context: Naoko gives a friendly cooking lesson at a noodle workshop.
purpose: Aunt teaching a small group how to make noodles by hand.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: 麺は、ようこねるんやで!
lines.en: Knead the noodles properly, you hear!
lines.style: Brassy, energetic Kansai accent. Sharp attack on the directive. Loud and clear like teaching a room. Genuine warmth underneath the volume—a woman who loves showing someone how it's done.

lines.speaker: aoi_barista
lines.jp: はい、おばさん、こうですか?
lines.style: Soft, eager tone. Slight upward lilt at the question, genuinely seeking approval. Warm and attentive, not nervous—the respect of learning from someone you trust.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.en: That's the way—put your strength into it!
lines.style: Animated, encouraging. Punchy delivery on the directive. Still loud, still Kansai, but now actively cheering her on. The pride of watching a student catch on.

lines.speaker: aoi_barista
lines.en: The flour's getting light and fluffy.
lines.style: Quiet observation, almost to herself. Warm noticing tone. Slight wonder in the voice—the small pleasure of watching technique work. Gentle exhale on the final word.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: 茹でるの、お湯たっぷりや。
lines.en: When you boil them, use plenty of water.
lines.style: Warm but firm Kansai delivery. Clear, practical instruction. Not loud this time—measured and assured, like someone who knows this matters and trusts her student to listen.

lines.speaker: aoi_barista
lines.style: Soft, genuine gratitude in the voice. Calm confidence now, not tentative. The quiet satisfaction of understanding. Slight nod in the delivery.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.style: Brassy, delighted laugh at the opening. Loud and proud, but softened by real affection. The warmth of someone watching a protégé get it right. Pride sits easy in this voice.
